chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
For the tongue of the mute, and the eye of the blind, and the manhood of the castrated man and his two testicles, is a third of the wergild.
ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation for the tongue of the mute and the eye of the blind according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies that the financial compensation (diyah) for injuries to the tongue of a mute, the eye of a blind, and the reproductive organs of a eunuch is one-third of the full blood money. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that these specific injuries are assessed based on their functional impact relative to the whole body, distinguishing them from injuries to fully functional limbs. It highlights the precision of early Shia legal tradition in categorizing bodily damages and their corresponding monetary values.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazaz, from Bureyd Bin Muawiya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘With regards to a tongue of the mute, and an eye of the blind, and one of castrated manhood and his testicles, is a third of the wergild’.
